models.name: Claude Opus 5.5
models.editorialNote: The model Anthropic recommends starting with for most workloads, built for long-running agentic coding and knowledge work. It carries the same context window and output limit as Fable 5.1 at less than half the price.

models.name: GPT-6 Luna
models.editorialNote: The cheapest model on this page at $0.10 in and $0.50 out, a third of DeepSeek V4.1 Flash's peak input rate and under half of its output rate, and it keeps the same context window and output limit as the two larger GPT-6 models. OpenAI aims it at focused, high-volume tasks.

models.name: GPT-6 Sol
models.editorialNote: The middle of OpenAI's lineup at a fifth of Astra's price, level with Claude Sonnet 5 on both input and output. OpenAI tells paid Codex users to pick it.

models.name: Grok 4.7
models.editorialNote: Its $6 output rate is the lowest of the four models here priced at $2 in, against $10 for Claude Sonnet 5 and GPT-6 Sol and $12 for Gemini 3.1 Pro, and its 500K window is half the million-token norm on this page. First-party access to X data is its clearest niche when freshness matters more than benchmark margin.

models.name: DeepSeek V4.1 Flash
models.editorialNote: The second cheapest model on this page after GPT-6 Luna, with the same 384K output limit as V4 Pro and the image input that V4 Flash lacked. The listed price is the peak rate, and off-peak hours are billed at half of it.

models.name: GPT-6 Astra
models.editorialNote: OpenAI's most capable model, aimed at complex reasoning, coding, and computer use. A prompt past 272K input tokens is billed at twice the input rate, which matters for anyone filling the million-token window.

models.name: Gemini 3.8 Flash
models.editorialNote: One of the two models here that take audio input, with a 64K output limit that is half of what the million-token models from Anthropic and OpenAI allow, and Google publishes no knowledge cutoff for it. The listed price holds through December 31, 2026 and doubles on January 1, 2027.

models.name: Muse Spark 1.3
models.editorialNote: Meta publishes neither an output limit nor a knowledge cutoff for it, two blanks no other provider here leaves at once except Mistral. Its $1.25 input rate sits between Claude Haiku 4.5 and Claude Sonnet 5, and Meta also sells a contributor tier at a lower price where prompts are used to improve its products.

models.name: Claude Fable 5.1
models.editorialNote: Anthropic's most capable model, which the company points at demanding reasoning and long-running agent work. It shares the highest price on this page with GPT-6 Astra, so I would reach for it where the quality of the answer matters more than the bill.

models.name: DeepSeek V4 Pro
models.editorialNote: The only text-only model on this page, and with V4.1 Flash it publishes the largest output limit here, 384K tokens, three times the 128K that Anthropic and OpenAI allow. The listed price is the peak rate, and off-peak hours are billed at half of it.

models.name: Claude Sonnet 5
models.editorialNote: A fifth of Fable 5.1's price with the same million-token window and 128K output limit, which is the trade I would take for most production traffic. Its January 2026 cutoff is the oldest of Anthropic's three million-token models here.

models.name: Mistral Medium 3.5
models.editorialNote: A 256K window, a quarter of the million-token norm here, and no published output limit or knowledge cutoff. Mistral calls it frontier-class, tunes it for agentic and coding work, and ships the weights under a modified MIT license, which is the part that matters if you need to run it yourself.

models.name: Gemini 3.1 Pro Preview
models.editorialNote: The only model on this page Google still labels a preview, released in February 2026, and its $12 output rate is the fourth highest here, after the $50 pair and Claude Opus 5.5. Pricing steps up past 200K tokens, audio input is native, and the thinking budget is adjustable per request.

models.name: Mistral Large 3
models.editorialNote: The only model on this page without a reasoning mode, and at $0.50 in and $1.50 out the third cheapest after GPT-6 Luna and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash. Open weights from a Paris-based lab, which is what makes it the option for a regulated EU deployment.

models.name: Claude Haiku 4.5
models.editorialNote: The smallest context window on this page at 200K and the oldest knowledge cutoff, at February 2025, but at $1 in and $5 out it is the cheapest Anthropic model here, which is where I would put batch classification, routing, and the high-volume edges of an agent graph.
